lead: Graeff-Hönninger, 5 October 2026, A-Drs.21(10)88-C, accidental THC exceedances and loss of certified-seed harvests

material_examined.scope: Full nine-page document, especially physical pp2 and4 (printed1 and3), pp6 and8 (printed5 and7). Official Bundestag copy independently reopened.
Exact 7 October 2025 bill BT21/2116, operative definition physical p3 and explanation pp5–6 and11–12.
Full four-page BT21/1188, especially government answer3 physical p2, independently reopened official primary.
Full January2026 three-page guidance; harvest release §3.5 physical p3.
Full three-page Annex4; document itself dated January2025 despite archive filename. Certified-seed requirement and notification sanction.

findings: The claim is explicit and supports the requested higher national THC definition. Government answer3 directly states that the alternative certified-seed/THC routes absorb natural fluctuations; this is a serious primary-source challenge rather than a mere absence of support.

The exact bill retains a certified-EU-seed alternative for other handling and separates the national definition from the unchanged EU direct-payment threshold. The bill itself repeats the crop-disqualification rationale in its explanatory memorandum. Agreement with a bill rationale does not establish factual correctness, but this is a disputed statutory/practical premise rather than an obvious misreading of an operative 0.3% destruction rule.

The author expressly acknowledges that the EU agricultural-payment threshold remains unchanged. It would be inaccurate to describe her as promising that the national amendment changes that funding rule.

The BLE harvest provision permits harvesting after actual sampling OR written release. Sampling alone is not contingent on a later low-THC analytical result in that provision. That weakens a suggestion that every exceedance necessarily prevents harvesting, but the guidance does not establish what can happen to a high-THC harvest under enforcement, processing, sale or food rules.

No primary destruction order, conclusive court treatment of this precise certified-seed scenario, or complete BLE enforcement explanation was established in this review. Absence of such evidence cannot establish that reported practical losses do not occur.
alternatives_tested: Formal certified-seed exemption may coexist with marketability restrictions or operational enforcement difficulties; harvest disqualification may describe practical unusability rather than formal loss of the statutory definition.

The summary speaks of a risk whereas the detailed paragraph uses categorical consequences. That is potentially overbroad but does not alone identify which legal or practical event the author is describing.
EU funding loss alone would not generally mean destruction of all crop value. However the document distinguishes that funding regime, so this possible conflation is not proved.
conclusion: Retain only as an unresolved legal/practice scope lead. Do not report proven absence of crop-loss risk from statutory alternatives or silence in a short administrative leaflet. A precise contemporaneous BLE explanation or a directly applicable high-THC certified-seed enforcement case would be needed to resolve it.
quote_policy: No additional original quotations reproduced; independent review refers to source locators to preserve per-source quote budget.
